questions.q: Per this lesson, what happens by default when the parent of a Lookup relationship is deleted?
options: The child record is not deleted -- the lookup field is simply cleared (or the delete can be blocked, depending on configuration)
The child record is automatically and immediately deleted, with no configuration needed
The entire object the child belongs to is deleted
Salesforce makes it physically impossible to ever delete a Lookup parent
questions.explain: Lookup is loosely coupled -- no automatic cascade delete happens the way it does with Master-Detail.

questions.q: What happens when the master record of a Master-Detail relationship is deleted?
options: Every detail record tied to it is automatically deleted too -- cascade delete, with no extra configuration
Nothing happens to the detail records at all
The detail records are only flagged for review, never deleted
Salesforce blocks the deletion in all cases
questions.explain: Cascade delete is automatic and non-optional on Master-Detail relationships.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say roll-up summary fields are only possible on Master-Detail relationships, not Lookup?
options: Master-Detail guarantees the relationship exists for every detail record, which a roll-up depends on; Lookup's optional link provides no such guarantee
Roll-up summary fields are actually possible on both relationship types equally
Lookup relationships don't support numeric fields at all
Roll-up summary fields are a deprecated feature no longer used in Salesforce
questions.explain: Because a Master-Detail child can't exist without its parent, Salesforce can safely calculate roll-ups on the parent.

questions.q: How is security handled differently between Lookup and Master-Detail relationships?
options: Master-Detail detail records inherit the master's security automatically; Lookup child records have independent security
Both relationship types always use fully independent, unrelated security
Both relationship types always inherit security identically
Security has nothing to do with relationship type in Salesforce
questions.explain: Inherited security is one of Master-Detail's defining, non-negotiable behaviors; Lookup security is independent.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why does knowing whether two objects are related by Lookup or Master-Detail matter for an analyst reading a report?
options: It tells you, before running a query, what kind of surprise a parent deletion could cause -- a real cascade-deleted drop in numbers vs. records silently losing their parent link
It has no practical effect on reports or dashboards at all
It only matters for Salesforce administrators, never for analysts
Relationship type only affects field labels, not actual record behavior
questions.explain: A Master-Detail cascade delete produces a real drop in counted records; a Lookup parent deletion just clears a field -- different diagnoses for the same-looking report change.
